name: nucbox-ownguest
status: DRAFT, HELD with v11 as the staged medium: v11 plus the NODE TREE enclave-5d's box acceptance harness imports (27 repository files at 8d82f67f, 15 npm packages by tarball with npm's integrity), the harness itself, and enclave-d1's WMISERVE-PROTOCOL.md. The harness has NOT run on the box. Also: the NEXT medium (7b9b04d6, on enclave-5d's initrd a1ff9864 whose ready line names the vsock transport). Not a release. This medium has NOT yet been booted on the NucBox. Host exclusion is NOT established (type 16: the root can map the guest's memory). With the PREVIOUS medium 4c387086, enclave-d1's dev-boot script served hello-world through the launcher's wmiserve (identity NOT verified: curl -k); the MANAGER cannot yet serve on this path (managerServing, pinned red).
about: Everything nucbox-k11 needs to boot OUR guest (the isolation/m3 monitor image) and serve one small app: the OpenHCL IGVM (profile igvm, the target, blocked on the Hyper-V role) and the same monitor image on the WSL kernel under the box's own launcher (profile hcs-dev, runnable today, development only). Version 12 (draft) = version 11 plus the node tree (windows/node, relay/tunnel.js and the relay verifiers it imports, isolation/contract, wasm/ipfs_fetch.py at enclave-d1's 8d82f67f) with node_modules assembled from 15 pinned npm tarballs, enclave-5d's hvlab-accept.mjs (8bb7d111), and enclave-d1's wmiserve line protocol (WMISERVE-PROTOCOL.md at 8d82f67f). Version 11 (draft) = version 10 with the next medium: enclave-5d's initrd a1ff9864 (6f1a9aff), whose ready line is 'MON ready control_port=9000 transport=hv_sock|virtio' and which refuses to start with no vsock transport; UKI 20a0e18e, ISO 7b9b04d6, disk.raw 23c52ecc. Version 10 (draft) = version 9 re-pinned on enclave-d1's cf640825 (the launcher states the partition kind wmi-openhcl-gen2 and the UEFI identity is the MEDIUM's hash; defects 16, 18, 19 closed; the dev-boot script that reached MON ready) and enclave-99's c6554c6c, carrying d1's dev-boot script and petri's hyperv.psm1 pinned so the boot is reproducible from the package, and d1's boot evidence quoted exactly. Version 9 (draft) = version 8 plus the uefi profile: the same guest as a standard UEFI payload (a read-only El Torito ISO; a VHDX fallback) under Microsoft's standard OpenHCL image, which this build starts while it does not start a linux-direct one (research E8). Version 8 (draft) = version 7 with enclave-d1's node at d1f4b745 (the hooks that import the bridge, appzone.mjs's isolated branch, main.mjs's data plane), enclave-5d's node-bridge.mjs 4cb8d54f (isolationPlan takes require, manager and appConfigCid), enclave-99's suites at 1d6d9b60 (node-bridge 6/6, appzone-hook), and the catalog versions as read on-chain, rebuilt byte for byte by the shipped isolationPlan. Version 7 = version 6 with enclave-5d's node-side bridge (node-bridge.mjs) and the splice client it imports (supervisor-splice.mjs, ws loaded lazily), both at e7ec6521 and imported by nothing on the box yet; 5d's datapath suite now runs its interop case (5/5, no skip). The manager stays at 72c82fc6: enclave-d1 has newer commits (0b49f6b6, 5a8a33e7) that this version does not pin. Version 6 = version 5 with enclave-d1's manager at 72c82fc6: the spawn path judges readiness behind its answer and writes status running with the transportKeySha256 the document was verified on, judging with the runtime identity object (defect 11), which the entry point reads from ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_IDENTITY, the image's runtime.json (defect 12; ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_ID alone is refused); image comes from the launcher's ready line; the 409 carries its id; HCS destroy by numeric id and answer correlation; the boundary accessor. Six functional suites are pinned with exact results. Version 5 = version 4 with enclave-d1's manager at 6d6c289e (ready.mjs fixed: defect 10, and the verdict carries transportKeySha256; /vms speaks guestd's contract: 201, status, boundary, relay, domainId, guestPort, image), enclave-5d's datapath at b339e9d4 (its lookup record uses transportKeySha256), and enclave-99's readiness test pinned with its exact result. Version 4 = version 3 with enclave-d1's manager at f4f10c84 (it creates the VM with -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL; ready.mjs) and the launcher rebuilt at 55494efa (/2 bundles load); the Hyper-V registry opt-in is a gating host check. Version 3 = version 2 with enclave-5d's datapath at 09b67414 (route identity from the view's tier; any safe id, the manager owning its ids). Version 2: the guest is enclave-5d's initrd 4610d594 (aef54ff7: /2 run mode, readiness, a launcher-named certificate name) and the IGVM around it; the app's answer is pinned to the byte; the datapath is pinned; the domain's attestation document is judged with enclave-d1's judge-hv. Built from existing artifacts plus igvmfilegen (seconds). windows/vbslike/pkg/README.md.

tier.name: T0-hv
tier.note: A Ryzen with no SEV-SNP. The root partition can read every guest's memory and the launcher signs the reports. Nothing served from this package is verified or host-excluded capacity.

hcs-dev.status: needs only Virtual Machine Platform and vmcompute: no role, no reboot; check.ps1 reports whether this host has them
hcs-dev.boundary: an HCS child partition: separated from other partitions, NOT from this host; development path only

igvm.status: needs the Hyper-V role (vmms, root\virtualization\v2 with Msvm_VirtualSystemSettingData.FirmwareFile, Get-VM) AND the host's AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile opt-in (bounded set-probe-restore procedure, authorized); check.ps1 reports whether this host has them
igvm.boundary: not established: this image has never been loaded (windows/vbslike/evidence/igvm-never-loaded-2026-09-24.md on windows/custom-vbs-like-hyperv)

manager.must: the manager's own start() issues New-VM with -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL or TrustedLaunch (checked on a recording host by pkg.mjs verify and by check.ps1)

measured: A Generation 2 VM created WITHOUT -GuestStateIsolationType accepts the FirmwareFile pin (ModifySystemSettings returnValue 0), reads it back, starts, and boots nothing: the worker never logs an IGVM load and nothing anywhere says why (enclave-d1, nucbox-k11, 2026-09-24).

Created WITH -GuestStateIsolationType OpenHCL or TrustedLaunch, the worker tries, and Worker-Admin event 5142 says: failed to load custom IGVM file because AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile registry key is not set (0x80070032).

IsolationType does NOT EXIST in this build's Msvm_VirtualSystemSettingData (26200.9457; reading it gives null, which v4-v7 recorded as 'reads EMPTY'); the type lives in GuestStateIsolationType. Also absent here: GuestStateLifetime, DefaultBootAlwaysAttempt, ManagementVtlFeatureFlags, GuestStateEncryptionPolicy (research E6).

With the key set and isolation type OpenHCL, the worker LOADS the pinned file: the in-box DLL pinned by our path is refused by our path (0x80070057), and our IGVM loads with no complaint; the partition then fails to start with a bare Worker event 12030 carrying no cause. 'Loading IGVM file from default location' is not about the pinned paravisor (enclave-d1, 18d569ee; research correction).

OpenHCL's boot log has no serial route on this build: openhcl_boot logs to serial only when the host describes a COM3 (petri: build >= 27653; this host 26200); ohcldiag-dev (kmsg over hvsocket, VTL2 running) is the only way in, and building it here needs the Windows SDK (a resources question for Steven) (research E7).
Secure Boot is not a factor: pinned VMs fail identically with it on and off. The manager turns it off, as the upstream guide does, because a guest image may need that.

uefi.status: needs the Hyper-V role and the AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile opt-in (bounded set-probe-restore procedure, authorized); check.ps1 reports whether this host has them
uefi.boundary: a DEV boot: a Gen2 VM under Microsoft's standard OpenHCL image. Host exclusion is NOT established, the tier stays T0-hv, and it must never be presented as final isolation

managerServing.measuredBy: win/manager-check.mjs on the pinned manager's own start(), recording host, 2026-09-25
managerServing.note: RED AS MEASURED (sent to enclave-d1 with lines, accepted): the manager's start() attaches no medium and sets no boot device, returns verifyImage()'s {sha256, bytes} of the FIRMWARE as image (the datapath compares a 64-hex string, so every route would be refused), and has no 9001 bind, 9000 load or relay, so no launcherKey and no relay and readiness is never judged. The dev-boot script + wmiserve did all of this once by hand. When the manager gains it, THIS PIN MOVES.

uefi.identity: partition.guestImageSha256 = the attached MEDIUM's sha256, hashed AT ATTACH (guest.iso's bytes on the DVD path, disk.raw's for the VHDX payload), with the UKI and its composition beside it; partition = wmi-openhcl-gen2, the LAUNCHER's word (isolation/m3/UEFI-BOOT.md at 4127789d; wmi-launcher.mjs uefiImageIdentity at fe56ad65). With Secure Boot off, systemd-stub honours ESP side-files and cmdline overrides; only a medium hash rules them out, and the guest's guards refuse them.
measured: DEV only, QEMU q35 + OVMF on KVM (warden-host): this ISO (7b9b04d6) boots past the guards and then REFUSES by name, 'MON ERROR no vsock transport: neither Hyper-V's (hv_sock) nor virtio's is present', and powers off, because the pinned WSL kernel has no virtio vsock transport. That is the guard working on KVM, not a boot. On the NucBox the same medium is expected to print transport=hv_sock; not yet measured.

ON THE NUCBOX, DEV BOOT (enclave-d1, uefi-dev-boot.ps1, log uefi-dev-boot-20260925-011023.log, read by enclave-53): this medium 4c387086, hashed at attach, under openhcl.bin 48773995, in enclave-uefi-20260925-011023 (Gen2, isolation OpenHCL, Secure Boot Off, boot order Drive only, no LoadOptions, vTPM absent, 1 vCPU, 2048 MiB). COM1 attached 454 ms after start. Console: 'MON snp=0 vcpus=1 memMiB=1965 boot_ms=308', the vsock module insmods failing harmlessly, 'MON boundary tier=t0-hv vmpl=n/a vmpl_floor=n/a vmpl0=n/a host_excluded=no', 'MON ready control_port=9000 snp=false'. Worker-Admin 18500 started successfully, 18601 successfully booted an operating system. Then the VM removed, the setting restored to Absent (verified), the live node unchanged (pid 8736), the six apps' answers identical before and after.

SERVED on the NucBox, DEV/INTEGRATION (enclave-d1, uefi-dev-boot.ps1 at 423fca4e, launcher c2cb0c10, medium 4c387086 hashed at attach, firmware 48773995, bundle 9c3d10f1, VM Gen2 type 16 Secure Boot off no vTPM one boot entry no LoadOptions 1 vCPU 2048 MiB with a SCSI controller added), verbatim: 'MON ready control_port=9000 snp=false' / {"step":"report-service","port":9001,"bound":true} / {"step":"load","ok":true,"id":1,"appSha256":"9c3d10f1450e17bc6a21478723193ef7e3da409afe353e264714cb801d180d45","agreed":true,"guestPort":40001} / {"step":"relay","ok":true,"tcp":19500,"guestPort":40001} / 'APP ANSWERED: Hello World!'. LIMITS (d1's): the guest's TLS was accepted with curl -k, so this shows the app SERVES and says nothing about identity (judge-hv on the handshake key is that check, not run here); type 16 is OpenHCL with NO isolation, the root can map the guest's memory: integration progress, not the isolation goal. d1's capture counted 14 body bytes; the pinned answer is 13 raw bytes (measured by wasmtime serve here and by enclave-99's box window), the extra one being the capture's trailing newline.

What that DEV boot does NOT show: host exclusion (the boundary line says host_excluded=no); attestation (no report was requested or signed); a bundle loaded or an app served; hv_sock reaching VTL0 through OpenHCL's relay. The control exchange (9000 load, 9001 signing, the 40000+id relay) for a WMI-created VM now EXISTS in the launcher (`wmiserve`, 1ba73a20) and was driven once by the dev-boot script; the MANAGER does not drive it yet (profiles.uefi.managerServing, pinned red), so no app is served through the node on this path.
Not measured on the NucBox: see windows/vbslike/pkg/uefi/README.md, 'Not yet measured under UEFI on the NucBox' (10 items, reviewed by enclave-99).

caveats: transportKeySha256 is populated WHEN a domain is judged ready: the spawn path judges readiness and writes status running with the key the document was verified on (82916eb8). A record may legitimately carry status starting with a null key, and the datapath refuses that (enclave-d1). Defect 11 (enclave-99): at 82916eb8 #judgeReadiness passed the runtimeId hash where judge-hv wants the runtime identity object, so no domain was ever judged ready; fixed at d9084612, where the Manager takes the identity and derives the id from it.

Defect 12 (found by enclave-53 reading d9084612): main.mjs constructed the Manager with runtimeId only, so a manager started the normal way pinned no runtime identity. Fixed at 72c82fc6: main.mjs reads the identity from ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_IDENTITY (point it at this package's guest/runtime.json; check.ps1 prints it) and refuses to start with only ENCLAVE_RUNTIME_ID. main-entry (enclave-99) is the pinned test of that entry point.

enclave-d1's line protocol for `vbslike-host wmiserve` (8d82f67f): invocation with --medium-sha256 REQUIRED (the medium as attached), one JSON object per step (launcher / report-service / load / relay / ready / closed; a missing later step is a failure), the four rules (hash disagreement destroys the domain; only a loaded app is signed; only that partition may ask; the relay never terminates TLS), the report's fields (medium hash, kernelSha256 omitted, the partition kind stated by the launcher, hostExcluded:false), and the hv_sock service-GUID prerequisite (os error 10013). The manager driver and this package name the same contract

enclave-d1's host side of the UEFI DEV boot, at 423fca4e 'the whole path, and the hv_sock service registration it needed': it drives wmiserve (report service, load, relay) and answered the app. enclave-53's review findings of 2026-09-25 were accepted by d1; see the commit for which have landed. Earlier text: the bounded set-probe-restore of AllowFirmwareLoadFromFile, petri's New-CustomVM definition, the medium hashed at attach, the read-back (one boot entry, no LoadOptions, Secure Boot off, vTPM absent), COM1 held from start, a watchdog. Run by enclave-d1 only. enclave-53's review findings of 2026-09-25 are open against it
